purpose: Player-specific offensive-environment writeups for the comparison engine. These notes explain the grade using actual quarterback, scheme, role, target-competition and protection context rather than generic tier language.

Ladd McConkey.environment_detail: Quarterback: Justin Herbert gives McConkey high-end accuracy and arm talent. Scheme/role: Mike McDaniel's motion, spacing and YAC-oriented concepts fit McConkey's separation and inside/outside versatility, keeping him positioned as a primary chain-moving target rather than a generic slot receiver. Target competition: the Chargers have perimeter options, including Tre' Harris and Quentin Johnston, but their roles are different from McConkey's route-winning target profile. O-line/protection: the unit has enough talent to support an efficient passing game, with health and continuity the main structural variables. Overall, the environment is very favorable because Herbert plus McDaniel specifically amplify what McConkey does best.

A.J. Brown.environment_detail: Quarterback: Drake Maye gives Brown a strong downfield and touchdown-producing quarterback environment. Scheme/role: Brown arrives in New England as the clear alpha perimeter receiver and should be featured on isolation routes, in-breaking concepts and high-value red-zone/deep targets rather than sharing an equal target hierarchy. Target competition: the supporting receivers can draw coverage and fill complementary roles, but there is no comparable established alpha who should prevent Brown from commanding the passing game. O-line/protection: protection quality matters because Brown's intermediate and downfield routes need time to develop, while the new-team transition adds some early continuity risk. The ceiling comes from pairing Maye's arm talent with Brown's target dominance.
